thread_analysis.thread_summary: [COMPANY] plans a Bluetooth registration for a Communications Terminal product line by combining an existing module QDID (MAYA-W1) and an existing host-stack QDID (Fluoride 1.5), covering HID, SPP, PAN, BNEP, HOGP, and ScPP profiles. The thread works through which profile ICS gaps require fresh PTS testing versus which can simply inherit the host stack's existing ICS, applies a specific TCW (ES-26007) to waive Core-layer Invalids from adding the new Profile (X2Core) definition, catches a self-contradictory pair of ICS values in the customer's own submission, and resolves registration-form mechanics for listing three same-module products under one registration with a unified Design Name. It ends with the customer choosing to fully align all profile ICS with the host stack's existing support (dropping HID11 and other extra requirements) to avoid new testing entirely, followed by a routine payment-processing status check.
all_questions_found: Is there an existing TCW that can waive the Core-layer Invalids expected from adding a new Profile (X2Core) definition while Including existing Controller Subsystem and Host Subsystem registrations without modifying their referenced QDIDs/DNs?

When Including a module QDID and a host-stack QDID together, which profiles already match the customer's desired ICS, and for which profiles does the gap require fresh PTS testing versus being acceptable to leave as inherited?
Is there a simpler way to check a host-stack QDID's supported profiles and ICS than importing an ICS Export file into a Qualification Workspace project?
Has the customer decided to drop HID11 from the product's scope, making HID11 PTS testing unnecessary?

Do SPP, ScPP, and BNEP need ICS verification if only their minimum required support is needed, given that an already-registered QDID guarantees at least that minimum as a condition of its own registration?
Does the host stack's existing HID, PAN, and HOGP ICS support actually meet the customer's required ICS features for those profiles?

If the customer ultimately decides to align all profile ICS with the host stack's existing support rather than pursue fresh testing for any gap, can the registration proceed entirely on a profile-testing exemption basis?
What additional registration delay should be expected once a TCW application is filed alongside the registration?
Does the customer's submitted ICS contain any internally inconsistent or self-contradictory values that need correcting before proceeding?
Can three separate products that share the same Bluetooth module and host stack all be listed together as the first models planned for sale on a single new registration?

Since the registration site treats the first-entered Product List name as the registration's Design Name, what should be entered as the Design Name when a single registration covers multiple distinctly-named products?
thread_analysis.key_technical_discussion: The thread covers several mechanics of combining existing module and host-stack registrations into a new product registration: using TCW ES-26007 to waive Core-layer Invalids that arise specifically from adding a new Profile (X2Core) definition while Including unmodified existing Controller Subsystem and Host Subsystem registrations; checking a host-stack QDID's actual supported ICS directly via its registration detail page (simpler than importing an ICS Export file into a temporary Workspace project); the principle that an already-registered QDID guarantees at least minimum-required ICS support for any profile it includes, removing the need to verify profiles where only baseline support is needed; catching a self-contradictory pair of mutually-exclusive ICS values in a customer's own ICS submission before they propagate into the registration; the registration-form mechanic where the first Product List entry becomes the registration's Design Name, requiring a deliberate, unified name choice when one registration covers multiple distinctly-named products; and the expected 2-5 business day registration delay caused by a TCW application requiring SIG administrator review before finalization.
thread_analysis.key_decision_logic: When combining an existing module QDID with an existing host-stack QDID, the decision of whether to pursue fresh PTS testing for a given profile depends on whether the gap between the customer's desired ICS and the host stack's actual supported ICS is 'non-negotiable' (requiring testing and replacing the inherited ICS with a fresh test report) or acceptable to leave as-is (in which case reusing the inherited ICS without testing is recommended); profiles needing only minimum/baseline support don't need this comparison at all, since an already-registered QDID guarantees that baseline as a condition of its own registration. A specific TCW (ES-26007) exists precisely for the case of adding a new Profile/X2Core definition on top of unmodified, already-Included Controller Subsystem and Host Subsystem registrations, and should be checked for applicability before assuming a Core-layer Invalid is unresolvable. Self-contradictory ICS values submitted by a customer (such as two mutually-exclusive items both marked supported) must be caught and corrected to a single consistent value before they are used as the basis for registration. For a registration covering multiple distinctly-named products sharing the same module and host stack, all model names can be listed together in the 'first model to sell' field, but a deliberate, unified Design Name should be chosen rather than defaulting to whichever product name happens to be entered first.
thread_analysis.risk_if_done_wrong: Assuming a Core-layer Invalid from adding a new Profile definition is unresolvable, without checking for an applicable TCW like ES-26007, would lead to unnecessary rework or an abandoned registration approach. Failing to catch a self-contradictory ICS value pair before registration could produce an invalid or rejected registration. Defaulting to whichever product name is entered first as the Design Name, without considering that the registration covers multiple distinctly-named products, could create a confusing or inaccurate registration record. Not accounting for the 2-5 business day delay from a TCW application could create unrealistic registration-completion expectations.
thread_analysis.consulting_takeaway: When combining a module QDID and a host-stack QDID, always check the host stack's actual ICS directly via its registration detail page before deciding which profiles need fresh testing, and treat profiles needing only minimum/baseline ICS as already covered without verification. Check for an applicable TCW (such as ES-26007) before assuming a Core-layer Invalid from adding a new Profile definition is unresolvable, but build in the resulting 2-5 business day SIG review delay when setting registration-completion expectations. Always review a customer's submitted ICS for internally self-contradictory values before using it. When a registration will cover multiple distinctly-named products sharing the same module and host stack, proactively choose a unified Design Name rather than letting the first-entered product name default into that role.
